name: @clossys/writer

capabilities.subQuestion: Does every voice claim trace to a derivation and field record, and is it internally consistent?
capabilities.worldClass: Voice is a governed record with full derivation and field coverage, never a style felt out per sentence.

capabilities.subQuestion: Is every piece of audience-facing copy a validated, addressable registry entry?
capabilities.worldClass: Every shipped sentence resolves from one validated registry entry by id — never typed ad hoc into a component.

capabilities.subQuestion: Does every claim-shaped or numeric sentence in shipped copy trace to an approved registry claim?
capabilities.worldClass: A currency amount, percentage, multiplier, or superlative sentence in live copy either matches a registered claim or carries a citation to one — never asserted bare.

capabilities.subQuestion: Does live, shipped copy still match its registry source and stay within its word-budget and fold rules?
capabilities.worldClass: Shipped copy never drifts silently from its registry source, and the above-the-fold word budget is enforced, not eyeballed.

capabilities.subQuestion: Is every piece of user-facing prose resolved from the registry by id, never typed directly into a component?
capabilities.worldClass: A rename is always cheap: renaming a piece of copy means editing one registry entry, never hunting every component that typed the sentence.

capabilities.subQuestion: Does the product have one governed tagline, pitch-length set, boilerplate, and FAQ that everything else derives from?
capabilities.worldClass: One governed messaging kit (tagline, short/medium/long pitch, short/medium/long boilerplate, FAQ) exists and every surface's short-form copy derives from it, rather than being improvised per surface.

description: The writer role: is it well said? A consumer-owned language system: voice rules, glossary and claims validation, addressable copy records, source traceability, locale coverage, and passage-layer composition — five gates reachable from one bin. Ships machinery and templates, never a consumer's actual copy or voice.
author: Clossys
